Hi Sophie —

Quick answers to the items you raised so the reference call can focus on operations rather than architecture:
- VoltGrid's deployment was private: control plane and token management ran in their VPC; payload telemetry was kept on-prem and only aggregated metrics were optionally sent to Redwood-hosted analytics. We can provide a short tech note to confirm the pattern.
- Network: primary wired LAN inside the warehouse with LTE as backup in a few sites; VoltGrid used periodic syncs and a small local KV cache for inference state, which kept live decisions local when connectivity dropped.
- Upgrades: rolling upgrades across gateways; downtime per gateway was sub-30s for the inference process; they scheduled full fleet upgrades weekly during low-load windows.
- Storage: local retention was configured to 30 days, aggregated metrics forwarded hourly. Costs were negligible vs. the infra savings from avoiding constant cloud inference.
